subject: combining different runs with different numbers of features

messages.author: 0c5ec2c4dfce1ca1
messages.subject: combining different runs with different numbers of features
parts:
Hello,

I am new to using Cardinal (and new to analyzing DESI MS data) and am trying to combine three different runs together into one object using cbind().  I thus far have been unable to combine all three together because the number of rows (features) do not match.  I can combine run1 and run2 fine, but then I cannot combine run3 with them (run 3 has more features).  I have tried using mzBin() followed by process() like this:
AgNp1_bin <-mzBin(AgNp1_neg, from = 100, to = 1199.925, resolution=28, units="ppm)
AgNp1_bin <- process(AgNp1_bin)
AgNp2_bin <-mzBin(AgNp2_neg, from = 100, to = 1199.925, resolution=28, units="ppm)
AgNp2_bin <- process(AgNp2_bin)
AgNp3_bin <-mzBin(AgNp3_neg, from = 100, to = 1199.925, resolution=28, units="ppm)
AgNp3_bin <- process(AgNp3_bin)

cbind(AgNp1_bin, AgNp2_bin, AgNp3_bin)

 but I still get the error that the number of rows don't match.  I am sure it is likely a simple fix, but I am not quite sure what to do next.  Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks
Nadia

messages.author: db2a70d9b31cb1f7
messages.subject: Re: combining different runs with different numbers of features
parts:
Hi Nadia,

the code looks good to me.

So I am just trying to speculate what could have gone wrong: Maybe one of the mzBin steps gave an error you overlooked? Maybe you obtain a hint about the problem by using dim() and/or mz() on each file before and after binning. Is the MSI data "continuous" or "processed" type? Just run "AgNp1_neg" and see if the first line is: An object of class 'MSProcessedImagingExperiment' or 'An object of class 'MSContinuousImagingExperiment'. Repeat for the other 2 datasets.

Best,
Melanie

messages.subject: Re: combining different runs with different numbers of features
parts:
Hi Melanie,

Thanks for your response.  The MSI data is of the "processed" type for each of the 3 datasets.  The data indeed were of different dimensions and for one sample the dimensions were the same as the original dataset -  I looked more closely and saw that for the one sample there was the following error:

Error: BiocParallel errors

1 remote errors, element index: 6

14 unevaluated and other errors

first remote error: unused argument (dots[[2]][[36873]])

I reran the command and it ran without any error and then cbind worked well.  Thank you for your suggestion!


Thanks

Nadia
